extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, regulated electric generating units (EGUs), environmental regulators, and stakeholders preparing or reviewing CAA section 111(d) state plans and compliance approaches
extracted.subtask_short: state plans for EGUs under CAA 111(d)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for states and regulated EGUs developing and implementing state plans under Clean Air Act section 111(d), including how to set standards of performance, when to apply remaining useful life adjustments, monitoring and reporting expectations, and available compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: In devising emissions limits for power plants, EPA first `determines' the `best system of emission reduction' that—taking into account cost, health, and other factors—it finds `has been adequately demonstrated.' The Agency then quantifies `the degree of emission limitation achievable' if that best system were applied to the covered source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and EPA must identify BSER (considering cost, health, and other factors) at the appropriate scale and then quantify achievable emission limitation; BSER selection underpins presumptive standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF (Remaining Useful Life) — applying less stringent standards
rubrics_metrics.description: States may invoke RULOF to apply a less stringent standard of performance to a particular affected EGU when the state demonstrates that the EGU cannot reasonably achieve the degree of emission limitation determined by the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RULOF is invoked, the state plan may set a less stringent standard for that EGU; however, 40 CFR 60.24a(f) requires that any standard pursuant to RULOF be no less stringent than necessary to address the fundamental difference identified under 40 CFR 60.24a(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Units for standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumptive standards of performance for coal-fired steam-generating affected EGUs and base load and intermediate load natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating affected EGUs are in units of lb CO2/MWh; the presumptive standard of performance for low-load natural gas-fired and oil-fired affected EGUs are in units of lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards derived using RULOF must be expressed in the same units applicable to the subcategory (lb CO2/MWh or lb CO2/MMBtu as appropriate); states should ensure unit consistency when crafting source-specific standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: State alternative methodology must achieve equivalent emission reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Should a state decide to establish a standard of performance for an affected EGU using a methodology other than that provided by the EPA in these emission guidelines, the state would have to demonstrate that the resulting standard of performance achieves equivalent emission reductions as application of the EPA's presumptive standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States bear the burden of demonstrating equivalence between their alternative methodology and EPA's presumptive standard; documentation and justification must be provided in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance flexibilities (emission averaging and trading)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the state plan incorporates compliance flexibilities like emission averaging and trading, an affected EGU must demonstrate compliance consistent with the expression of the respective flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA has authorized trading/averaging in prior emission guidelines; when states adopt such flexibilities they must specify how compliance is measured and demonstrated consistent with the chosen flexibility (e.g., allowance accounting, aggregate demonstrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone reporting requirements for certain coal-fired EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: The milestone reporting requirements for affected coal-fired steam generating EGUs in the medium-term subcategory and those relying on a shorter remaining useful life for a less-stringent standard of performance pursuant to RULOF are authorized under both CAA sections 114(a) and 111(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting/milestones are required to ensure predicate conditions for source-specific standards (e.g., RULOF) are satisfied; states must include and enforce such reporting where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plans must include enforceable commitments to cease operation when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with CAA section 111(d)(1), state plans must include commitments to cease operation as necessary for the implementation and enforcement of standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating conditions within the control of a designated facility that are relied on for RULOF must be included as enforceable requirements in state plans; adherence to these commitments is necessary to maintain the level of emission reduction required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of retirement/shutdown dates as federally enforceable measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement dates associated with standards of performance (when relied upon) must be included in state plans and become federally enforceable upon EPA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past guidance and rules have required that retirement dates or enforceable shutdown commitments be incorporated into state plans or SIPs when used as the basis for standards or controls; states should follow precedents for enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline emission rate calculation for existing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline emission rate for existing sources is the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation data for a given affected EGU from any continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to the date the final rule is published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and sources must use a continuous 8-quarter period within the most recent 5 years of Part 75 data to set baseline emission rates; selection and documentation of the period are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS monitoring and mass balance approach (subpart RR, subpart VV / ISO 27916:2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both subpart RR and subpart VV (CSA/ANSI ISO 27916:2019) require an assessment and monitoring of potential leakage pathways; quantification of inputs, losses, and storage through a mass balance approach; and documentation of steps and approaches used to establish these quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring for CO2 storage must include leakage pathway assessment, mass-balance quantification of inputs/losses/storage, and documented methodologies; states/facilities should follow the referenced ISO standard and subpart-specific definitions and termination criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in CCS mass-balance/ leakage definitions and reporting discontinuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary differences relate to the terms in their respective mass balance equations, how each defines leakage, and when facilities may discontinue reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities and states must understand subpart-specific definitions and criteria for discontinuing reporting and apply the correct mass-balance terms and leakage definitions for the chosen regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of 'other factors' beyond costs in RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Other factors' may include facility-specific circumstances and factors that the EPA did not anticipate and consider in the applicable emission guideline that make achieving the EPA's degree of emission limitation unreasonable for that facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking RULOF, states may cite non-cost factors (facility-specific circumstances) in addition to cost; these must be identified and justified in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability mechanisms and temporary extension of retirement dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability mechanism described ... is specific to reliability and can be used to extend the date by which a source plans to cease operating by up to 1 year. States may also elect to include the short-term reliability mechanism in their plans to address grid emergency situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States can include short-term reliability measures and an extension mechanism in plans to address grid emergencies; the mechanism can extend planned cessation dates (up to one year for the reliability mechanism) and should be clearly articulated in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with NERC reliability standards and planning authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The North American Electric Reliability Corporation's (NERC) definition of 'Planning Authority' and applicable NERC Reliability Standards (e.g., EOP-011-2) provide expectations for coordination of transmission, resource plans, and reliability practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans and EGU operators should coordinate with NERC Planning Authorities and apply relevant reliability standards and technical guidance when evaluating reliability impacts and justifying reliability-related measures in state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSD program pollutant definition and thresholds (regulated NSR pollutant)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the PSD program, 'regulated NSR pollutant' includes any pollutant for which a NAAQS has been promulgated ('criteria pollutants') and any other air pollutant that meets the requirements of 40 CFR 52.21(b)(50). Some of these non-criteria pollutants include greenhouse gases, fluorides, sulfuric acid mist, hydrogen sulfide, and total reduced sulfur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability analyses (e.g., for NSR/PSD) must treat greenhouse gases and other qualifying pollutants as regulated NSR pollutants where thresholds are met; sources should evaluate potential applicability and thresholds accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic minor limitation as an enforceable strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A synthetic minor limitation is a legally and practicably enforceable restriction that has the effect of limiting emissions below the relevant level and that a source voluntarily obtains to avoid major stationary source requirements, such as the PSD or title V permitting programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources may pursue enforceable permit limits or operational restrictions to remain below major source thresholds; such limitations must be legally enforceable and practically enforceable to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: BACT constraint relative to CAA sections 111 and 112
rubrics_metrics.description: In no event shall application of 'best available control technology' result in emissions of any pollutants which will exceed the emissions allowed by any applicable standard established pursuant to [CAA Section 111 or 112].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BACT determinations must be consistent with applicable emissions standards; see EPA BACT guidance documents (e.g., New Source Review Workshop Manual, PSD and Title V permitting guidance for GHGs) for recommended approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of discount rates and SC-CO2 methodology in regulatory analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetized climate benefits are discounted using a 2 percent discount rate, consistent with the EPA's updated estimates of the SC-CO2. OMB's Circular A-4 update recommended general application of a 2 percent rate to discount social costs and benefits and consideration of the shadow price of capital when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory analyses should use the updated 2% discount rate for monetized climate benefits (with discussion of alternatives and the rationale); documentation should explain rate choice and its implications for benefits estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic modeling and sensitivity analyses (IPM sensitivity runs)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA examined the final rules under a variety of different assumptions regarding demand, gas price, and contemporaneous rulemakings and determined that those alternative projections, inclusive of CCS buildout and cost profiles, would not alter any BSER design parameters selected in this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should perform sensitivity analyses (e.g., using IPM) across demand, fuel price, and rule interaction assumptions; documentation should show whether alternative assumptions would change BSER or other key determinations.
